watch.summary.back: This video was made at the Smithsonian Folklife Festival in Washington, D.C., United States. This festival invites people from many communities. They share their music, dances, crafts, and food. In this video, people at the festival talk about why sharing culture is important. Sharing culture helps people get to know each other. Sharing culture also helps them see the world in a new way. Sharing culture can help people stay strong in hard times and feel joyful in happy times. Each speaker gives their own view. No one person speaks for a whole culture. When you share respectfully, you listen to the people who practise a tradition. You also give them credit/recognition.
watch.summary.source: This video was made at the Smithsonian Folklife Festival in Washington, D.C., in the United States. The festival invites people from many communities. They share their music, dance, crafts and food. In the video, people at the festival talk about why sharing culture matters. Sharing culture helps people learn about each other. It helps them see the world in new ways. It can help people stay strong in hard times and feel joy in good times. Each speaker gives their own view. No one person speaks for a whole culture. When you share with respect, you listen to the people who practise a tradition. You also give them credit.

read.sections.0.text.back: A tradition is an activity that is done together and repeated over time. A tradition can be a meal, a song, a game, a skill, or a celebration. Many traditions mark important times in the year. Nowruz is the new year in spring. Millions of people in many countries celebrate Nowruz, from southeast Europe to Central Asia. People clean up, eat special dishes together, and enjoy music and dance. The shared meal event in the evidence is also a tradition. The elder says the event is important because people can meet, teach each other, and welcome each other.
read.sections.0.text.source: A tradition is a practice that people share and repeat over time. It can be a meal, a song, a game, a skill or a celebration. Many traditions mark an important time of year. Nowruz is a spring new year. Millions of people celebrate it in many countries, from south-east Europe to Central Asia. People clean, share special meals and enjoy music and dance. The community meal in the evidence is a tradition too. The elder says it matters because people meet, teach and welcome each other.

read.sections.0.simpler.source: A tradition is a thing people do again and again, for many years. It can be a meal, a song or a game. Many traditions mark a special time of year. Nowruz is a new year in spring. People in many lands celebrate it. They clean, share food and dance. The meal in the evidence is a tradition too. The elder says it helps people meet, teach and welcome others.

read.sections.1.text.back: Many traditions help older people hand down knowledge to younger people. This is called inheritance/passing down (pewarisan). In Korea, families and neighbours make kimchi together at the end of autumn. This tradition is called kimjang. They share the kimchi out to houses and exchange ideas. In North Africa, people learn to make couscous by watching and copying others. They eat it together at big family and community events. In Tonga, big groups perform lakalaka. Lakalaka is a dance with sung speeches about history and values. In the evidence, a young volunteer learns to make bread and wants to teach it next year.
read.sections.1.text.source: Many traditions help older people pass knowledge to younger people. This is called transmission. In Korea, families and neighbours make kimchi together in late autumn. This tradition is called kimjang. They share the kimchi between homes and swap ideas. In North Africa, people learn to make couscous by watching and copying others. They eat it together at big family and community events. In Tonga, large groups perform the lakalaka. It is a dance with sung speeches about history and values. In the evidence, a young helper learns to make the bread and wants to teach it next year.

read.sections.1.simpler.back: Traditions help older people teach younger ones. This is called passing down (pewarisan). In Korea, people make kimchi from vegetables. They make it in a big crowd in autumn. Then they share the kimchi. In North Africa, people learn to cook couscous. Couscous is a food made of small grains. People watch other people, then copy. In Tonga, big groups sing and dance lakalaka. Its song tells about the past. In the evidence, a young volunteer learns to make bread.
read.sections.1.simpler.source: Traditions help older people teach younger people. This is called transmission. In Korea, people make kimchi from vegetables. They make it in a big group in autumn. Then they share it. In North Africa, people learn to cook couscous. It is a dish of tiny grains. They watch others and copy them. In Tonga, big groups sing and dance the lakalaka. The songs tell about the past. In the evidence, a young helper learns to make bread.

read.sections.2.heading.back: Traditions can change and stay important
read.sections.2.heading.source: Traditions can change and still matter

read.sections.2.text.back: Traditions are not frozen in the past. People adapt traditions to fit new times. This year, the meal event added a vegetarian dish and started earlier, so that more people could take part. The new neighbour says that with the earlier time, they could come for the first time. Changes like this can help a tradition keep the same purpose: meeting, teaching, and welcoming. It would be better if the group talked about what is kept and what is changed. Not everyone in one community follows the same tradition or gives it the same meaning. No tradition is better than another tradition.
read.sections.2.text.source: Traditions are not frozen in the past. People adapt them to fit new times. This year, the meal adds vegetarian dishes and starts earlier, so more people can take part. The new neighbour says the earlier time means they can come for the first time. A change like this can help a tradition keep its purpose: to meet, teach and welcome. It helps when the group talks about what to keep and what to change. Not everyone in a community follows the same traditions or gives them the same meaning. No tradition is better than another.

read.sections.2.simpler.back: Traditions do not always stay the same. People adapt traditions to fit new times. This year, there is food without meat. The event also starts earlier. Now the new neighbour can come. So, the meal event still has the same purpose. The event still helps people meet and welcome other people. The group can discuss what they want to keep. People in one group can have different habits. No tradition is better than another.
read.sections.2.simpler.source: Traditions do not stay the same forever. People adapt them to fit new times. This year, the meal has food with no meat. It also starts earlier. Now a new neighbour can come. So the meal keeps its purpose. It still helps people meet and welcome others. The group can talk about what to keep. People in a group may not all do the same things. No tradition is better than another.

One of the changes is that the meal event now starts earlier. This can help because a new neighbour could come for the first time. The vegetarian dish can also let more people eat together. So, the changes can help the meal event keep the same purpose. The committee should also ask people which part matters most to them.
